summary: Fifth review round. Task scope was to decisively re-verify F-013 (the duplicate-publish-preview-artifact issue that recurred, unfixed, through rounds 3 and 4 despite being 'fixed' each time) via repeated time-gapped checks, carry forward F-001/F-002/F-009/F-010/F-011/F-012 (rounds 1-3, already clean), confirm F-014/F-015/F-016 (round 4's findings) are genuinely fixed, and do one more honest deep-structural pass for a possible 5th leak class. All of this round's checks came back clean. F-013: ran `find candidate/publish-preview -regex '.* [0-9]\(\.[a-z]*\)?$'` three separate times with real wall-clock gaps of ~8-9 minutes between each (not just the requested 20-30s) — 0 hits every time, and a full recursive directory listing (98 entries) matches contract §5a's exact expected shape for all 8 objects + _registry.json with no extras, no numbered duplicates, no empty directories. Also independently corroborated the producer's root-cause account (macOS File Provider/iCloud Drive sync racing a bulk-delete-then-recreate pattern) via `xattr -l` (com.apple.provenance present on the run directory) and `brctl status` (an active, caught-up CloudDocs sync daemon) rather than taking the narrative on faith — this time the story and the evidence both hold. F-014 (ENT-ID tokens), F-015 (dead-pointer field names/internal filenames), and F-016 (internal claim-taxonomy vocabulary 'normativity'/'EXAMPLE_ONLY'/etc.) all independently re-checked at 0 instances across the full candidate/publish-preview/** tree. F-001/F-002/F-009/F-010/F-011/F-012 (rounds 1-3) all reconfirmed clean via fresh greps, no regression. For the deeper structural pass invited by this round's task framing, two non-obvious angles were investigated in real depth rather than more pattern-matching on already-known leak classes: (1) whether any checklist check uses a KNOWN_DEFECT-status KB item as a STRONG oracle (forbidden per contract C5) — mechanically recomputed oracle_strength independently for all 369 checks across all 10 checklists from each check's own feature-scoped kb_id resolution; found 0 violations (13 checks do cite KNOWN_DEFECT items, but every one is explicitly labeled '[Regression-watch]'/'KHÔNG dùng làm oracle đúng/sai' and capped at BASELINE/NONE, never STRONG — a deliberate, consistently-applied, well-labeled design, not a defect; two apparent violations surfaced on a first pass turned out to be this reviewer's own script bug — a kb_id-namespace collision across sibling feature shards that share the literal id 'KB-008' with completely unrelated content, resolved incorrectly before the feature-scoping was fixed); (2) whether bootstrap-request.json's role=null admission (contract C0-DOC: 'role=null => MỌI KB item phải mang scope.role: unspecified') was actually honored, since the published items overwhelmingly carry specific roles (merchant/buyer/shopper/staff) rather than 'unspecified' — traced this to a deliberate, upfront-documented design in bootstrap-request.json's own note (per-claim role_stated set when determinable from doc content, 'unspecified' reserved for genuinely undeterminable items, plus an object-level NEEDS_CONFIRMATION OQ wherever a doc set spans more than one role) and verified it is applied correctly and consistently: the object-level role-ambiguity OQ is present on exactly the 4 objects whose own KB items actually span merchant+buyer (discount-offers, variant-swatches, translate-offers, analytics) and correctly absent on the 4 objects that are 100% single-role (ask-for-review, onboarding-dashboard, ai-offer-creation, translate-portal). Neither investigation surfaced a new defect; both are reported in coverage_findings for transparency rather than silently passed over, since a genuinely clean result after this much digging is itself a meaningful finding worth stating plainly. No new findings this round. All prior findings (F-001 through F-016) confirmed closed.
